chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man performs Hajj alone (Hajj al-Qiran or Hajj al-Ifrad contextually implying combining or intending one then changing), then he circumambulates the House and runs between Safa and Marwa, then it occurs to him to make it an Umrah. He said: 'If he entered into the state of Ihram (labba) after running (between Safa and Marwa) before shortening (his hair/cutting), he has no Mut'ah (compensation Umrah).' And similarly for the Mu'tamir (one performing Umrah then Hajj): if he entered Ihram before shortening, his Mut'ah is invalidated. And if he had entered Ihram initially with both Umrah and Hajj, he narrated that (it is valid).

key_terms.لَبَّى: Entered the state of Ihram / Declared intention

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim changes their intention from Hajj to Umrah after performing Tawaf and Sa'i but before cutting their hair?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the critical juncture in Hajj rituals where the validity of the 'Umrah al-Mut'ah' (or compensatory Umrah) hinges on whether the pilgrim has already performed Qasr (hair cutting) after the initial Tawaf and Sa'i. It establishes that once the physical act of Qasr is completed, the intention is fixed, preventing the conversion of the act into a different type of Hajj or Umrah, thereby preserving the integrity of the ritual sequence. This ruling is essential for understanding the flexibility and rigidity within Shia fiqh regarding the three types of Hajj (Tamattu', Qiran, and Ifrad).
